{{Short description|Mythological rock in Japan}}
[[File:People praying at the Kaname-ishi rock, which pins downs a giant catfish and prevents it from moving and causing earthquakes (13899051674).jpg|thumb|Painting of people praying at the rock for protection from earthquakes.]]
'''Kaname-ishi''' ({{wikt-lang|ja|要石}}, perhaps "foundation stone" but maybe more aptly "cap stone"){{sfnp|Smits|2009|pp=10–11}}{{sfnp|Ouwehand|1964|pp=67–72}} is a mythological rock that was believed to hold down the [[Japanese archipelago]]. It was believed that when it was jostled or disturbed, it caused earthquakes. It is located in [[Kashima, Ibaraki]].{{sfnp|Smits|2009|pp=10–11}}

Many earthquakes were believed to have been caused by the catfish [[Namazu]] which dwelt near it. The catfish was later restrained by [[Takemikazuchi]], protecting against earthquakes.{{sfnp|Smits|2009|pp=10–11}}{{sfnp|Ouwehand|1964|pp=67–72}} When the [[Takemikazuchi]] lets his guard fall, Namazu thrashes about and agitates the stone, causing violent earthquakes<ref>{{Cite web |title=Untitled (Monster Catfish, Kashima Deity, and the Kaname-ishi Stone) |url=https://collections.rom.on.ca/objects/2542907/untitled-monster-catfish-kashima-deity-and-the-kanameish;jsessionid=03D25813E22012AD964C6B7C2F503355 |access-date=2023-10-18 |website=collections.rom.on.ca |language=en}}</ref>

In the ''[[Namazu|namazu-e]]'' or catfish prints of the [[Edo period]], Takemikazuchi/Kashima is depicted attempting to subdue the catfish, protect the stone, and prevent [[earthquake]]s.<ref name="ashkenazi">{{cite book |last=Ashkenazi |first=Michael |url=https://archive.org/details/handbookofjapane0000ashk |title=Handbook of Japanese Mythology |publisher=ABC-CLIO |year=2003 |isbn=9781576074671 |page=[https://archive.org/details/handbookofjapane0000ashk/page/266 266] |url-access=registration}}</ref><ref name="Ouwehand2">{{cite book |last1=Ouwehand |first1=Cornelis |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1P4UAAAAIAAJ&pg=PA57 |title=Namazu-e and Their Themes: An Interpretative Approach to Some Aspects of Japanese Folk Religion |last2=Logunova |first2=Vera Vasil'evna |publisher=Brill Archive |year=1964 |pages=57–}}, gives sword as "Itsu-no-o habari"</ref> The paintings are believed to give protection against earthquakes themselves, and had a massive increase in popularity.<ref>{{Cite web |title=［Catfish and the Keystone (Namazu to Kanameishi)］ |url=https://www.library.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/portals/0/edo/tokyo_library/english/modal/index.html?d=5413 |access-date=2023-10-18 |website=www.library.metro.tokyo.lg.jp}}</ref>
